title: Team Ukraine accuses International Paralympic Committee of ‘systematic pressure’
content:
The National Paralympic Committee of Ukraine (NPC) has accused the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) of applying “systematic pressure” to their athletes and staff.

The NPC criticised what they called a “very special partnership” between IPC and the NPCs of Russia and Belarus, while citing four examples of the “critical and shameful” manifestations of the international governing body’s bias in a statement on Wednesday.

This included claiming Ukraine’s daily team meeting was inadmissible, removing their flag from the athletes’ residence, forcing biathlon gold medalist Oleksandra Kononova to remove her earrings before standing on the podium and “cynical and unlawful” behaviour towards cross-country skier Taras Rad’s family.

The IPC said on Thursday, however, that they were “surprised” by the statement “because we’ve received no feedback from them through the regular chef de mission meetings”.

“While we are empathetic to the situation faced by Ukrainian people, that empathy does not stretch to allowing NPC Ukraine to break the rules that govern these Games,” their statement continued.

“With regards to accusations of preferential treatment, NPC Ukraine has zero evidence to support this claim. The IPC works closely with all NPCs and offers no preferential treatment.”

Ukraine’s NPC said they had hung the national flag on the team residence, but it was forced to be removed and hung instead where it was “less visible”.

“We like this flag because this symbolises our good results,” Valerii Sushkevych, the head of the Ukraine NPC, told The Athletic. “We asked the representative organising committee, ‘is it possible to (have) this flag in this place?’ And some hours later, they say ‘it is against the point of regulation of IPC.’

“We waited two days (for an explanation), and during these two days we tried to find this point that it’s not possible to (have) on the building a flag, we can’t find it.”

The Milan Cortina organising committee said in a statement that the relocation was due to “Village regulations, which provide that NPCs may display national flags only in the residential areas they occupy”, instead of the “communal space” where the flag was initially hung.

The 35-year-old biathlon gold medalist was told to remove her earrings that said ‘stop war’ on them before she collected her medal. The podium is one of a number of protected areas at the Games, in/on which athletes are not permitted to make a protest.

“A member of staff noticed these earrings, realised it would most likely breach our supplementary regulations on demonstrations, the rules that are in accordance with the rules received from the IPC for these Games,” IPC spokesperson Craig Spence said. “The situation was recognised and, for us, that was the end of the matter.”

Ukraine’s NPC also condemned the alleged treatment of the family of Taras Rad, the bronze medallist in the men’s individual sitting biathlon event on Sunday. They say that his family had neck scarves (which featured the Ukrainian coat of arms) and a Ukraine flag (which had been signed by other Ukrainian Paralympic athletes) taken away from them.

“It’s repression. So terrible,” Sushkevych told The Athletic. “These Ukrainian athletes come here to defend peace. Understand that the IPC say (this is) about politics. Our efforts to fight for peace and against the war is not political. We want to live without war, without rockets and drones.”

The Games’ organising committee said that the security thought the flags “may have contained political messaging” but they “could not verify the meaning of the text” on the flags.

“As … it may have contained political messaging, which is not permitted under Games regulations, the spectators were asked to enter the venue without the scarves,” it confirmed.

Ukraine’s NPC said they had been put under “pressure” about the “inadmissibility” of their team meeting which is “prohibited by an unclear document or regulation”. They said the team meets for “10-15 minutes in the common hall (of their shared residence)” to plan the day.

The organising committee said in response that “NPCs are also able to book dedicated rooms within the Village to host meetings, ensuring that common areas remain available for all delegations” and “Milano Cortina 2026 works closely with all teams to accommodate meetings of different sizes”.

Russia were given six and Belarus four “bipartite” spots for athletes to compete under their own flag in alpine and cross-country skiing and snowboard. This marked the end of a 12-year period where, first for state-sponsored doping and later following the invasion of Ukraine, Russian and Belarusian athletes were not permitted to compete under thier own flags at the Winter Paralympics.

Ukraine have won 10 medals so far this Games, with three golds, two silvers and five bronzes. It is more total medals than Russia (six) though they have more golds (four), while Belarus have two medals from cross-country skier Raman Svirydzenka (one gold, one bronze).
